simple.meaning: זִיז (zîyz) is a Hebrew action word meaning “fulness of the breast; also a moving creature.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in Psalms, Isaiah, beginning at Psalms 50:11. The surrounding contexts include mountain.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to זִיז (H2123) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: זִיז (zîyz) / H2123 is traced through Psalms 50:11, Psalms 80:14, Isaiah 66:11 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: fulness of the breast; also a moving creature
definitions.full: H2123. ziyz I. זִיז noun masculine Psa 80:14 collective moving things (i.e. beasts) (etymology & exact meaning still rather dubious, compare Che OP 472 and on Psa 50:11 ; Thes and others v זוז ; De 50:11 compare Assyrian zizânu , collective reptiles , Dl S. 74 f. from a זִאזֵא compare move to and fro, agitate (compare זוע ); others compare Assyrian zâzu , abundance see II. זוז , so even Di Isa 66:11 ; this hardly suits Psa 80:14 ; זִיזָא ᵑ7 worm ); **on Assyrian zîzê , teats , see RFHarper AJSL xiv (1897-1898), 174 . — only construct שָׂדַי זִיז 50:11 the moving things of the field , as all known to ׳י (|| הָרִים עוֺף ; also in 50:10 חַיְתוֺיָֿ֑עַר , etc.); figurative of enemies of Israel 80:14 (|| מִיָּ֑עַר חֲזִיר ). II. זִיז noun [masculine] abundance, fulness : only כְּבוֺדָהּ מִזִּיז Isa 66:11 that ye may suck out and be delighted, from the abundance of her glory (i.e. of Jerusalem) (so Di and others; > Che critical note, and OP 472 f. Brd (compare Ew 'Euter' ), who compare vulgar Arabic zîza , udder (breast, teat); this suits verb תָּמֹצּוּ and || מִשֹּׁד וּשְׂבַעְתֶּם תִּינְקוּ , but is dubious in Hebrew, perhaps not Shemitic, see Dozy i. 619 a and references ; also Lag Proph. Chald. who proposes, plausibly, מִבִּיזִ , compare Aramaic PS 502 , ביזא ; Arabic pap ).
